The ring-regular-module and Fitting decomposition reduce maxima to local nilpotency. At odd p, direct binomial divisibility gives S^(p^d)/p of exact S-order p^(d-1), and induction increases index by phi(p^d) per extra p-adic exponent. For p=2, the B=J+2W identity and its exact half-cycle S-adic order give 2^(d-1)(a+1). Odd n/p-odd is invertible and the d=0 edge cases follow. The unit basis vector generates the regular module and attains the index. Independently calculated 52 local nilpotency indices for p in {2,3,5,7,11}, d≤3 and a≤3, all matching. This numerical sample supports but does not replace the full ring proof.
